scope: Bounded second search for direct published Malkangiri resident/Adivasi perspectives on DAMaN or represented health-access experience. No outreach, no full-film viewing, no canonical edits.

kb_query.result: Existing district banking entry; no relevant resident narrative located by query_research.

queries_attempted: Malkangiri Daman film tribal villagers perspective healthcare

findings.title: Miles to go: In these tribal regions of Odisha, the nearest health clinic is jungles & rivers away
findings.access: Full HTML opened and read; opening account rechecked. Author byline not displayed in extracted page. Aishwarya Mohanty is explicitly photo credit; do not infer authorship from that.
findings.kind: Reported first-person resident testimony about healthcare access, not film reception
findings.locator: Opening paragraphs before Distance & healthcare-seeking behaviour; extracted lines 49–62.
findings.usable_claim: The report identifies Raja Kirsani (name changed) as a Bonda resident of Sanuguda village, Badadural Gram Panchayat, Malkangiri. He describes more than three hours walking to care because ambulances cannot reach the village.
limits: A dated reported personal experience, not a representative survey or a current service audit.
Reported deaths in his family were explicitly undiagnosed; do not identify malaria as cause.
The report does not discuss his response to DAMaN.
Other named residents in Tanda are in Rayagada, not Malkangiri.
findings.author_verification: Root search result for exact Raja Kirsani returned the AMP article with explicit Aishwarya Mohanty byline; direct AMP open cache miss, normal article full text opened. Indexed byline, not inference from photo credit.
findings.funding_disclosure: Article states support by Health Systems Transformation Platform, HSTP Health Journalism Fellowship 2022.

findings.title: DAMaN, a spark in the dark
findings.author: Atri Prasad Rout
findings.access: Full HTML opened independently, including paragraphs 90–100.
findings.locator: Paragraph on strengths becoming weaknesses, extracted line98; craft praise lines90–97.
findings.usable_claim: Rout admires filmmaking but argues the single-character structure risks an outsider-saviour story.
limits: A named critic’s reading, not resident testimony or community consensus.
Do not adopt packed-house or commercial claims without separate evidence.

findings.title: Doctorhood, Mosquitos and the Adivasis: How DAMaN obfuscates the politics of public health in Odisha
findings.author: Pradyumna Behera
findings.locator: Representation argument in middle and concluding paragraphs; extracted lines74–94.
findings.usable_claim: Behera argues that doctor-centred storytelling gives insufficient space to Adivasi agency and the history of unequal healthcare access.
limits: Author note identifies a PhD student at IIT Bombay; do not infer resident or Adivasi identity.
Broader historical, caste and medical assertions were not independently checked in this pass.
No fresh film viewing supports adopting scene interpretations as our own.

findings.title: In remote tribal habitations, age-old health practices takes precedence amid stiff challenges
findings.locator: Andrahal opening and unnamed healer, lines71–72.
findings.usable_claim: Includes an unnamed Andrahal healer’s experience of changing availability of plants.
limits: Do not infer medical efficacy or generalise across communities.
ASHA testimony in same article is worker evidence, not a substitute for resident testimony.

access_limited_leads.title: How baby Mrutyunjay was born in Malkangiri
access_limited_leads.access: Search result returned extensive text, but direct page open returned403. Legitimate older route https://wagtail.ruralindiaonline.org/en/articles/how-baby-mrutyunjay-was-born-in-malkangiri/ returned cache miss. Not claimed as fully inspected primary article.
access_limited_leads.decision: Do not use as article evidence in this pass; retain lead for later accessible original.

recommended_one_amendment.placement: After the worker-perspectives paragraph, before the paragraph beginning A cinema story and a programme history.
recommended_one_amendment.paragraph: A resident’s account brings those access barriers closer. In a 2023 Down To Earth report, a Bonda resident of Sanuguda in Malkangiri, identified under the changed name Raja Kirsani, described walking for more than three hours to reach care because ambulances could not reach his village. His testimony concerns healthcare access, not a response to DAMaN.[^resident]
recommended_one_amendment.footnote: [^resident]: Down To Earth, [Miles to go: In these tribal regions of Odisha, the nearest health clinic is jungles & rivers away](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/governance/miles-to-go-in-these-tribal-regions-of-odisha-the-nearest-health-clinic-is-jungles-rivers-away-88765), 14 April 2023, opening account of Raja Kirsani (name changed), Sanuguda, Malkangiri. A dated reported personal experience; not a community survey or film-reception interview.
recommended_one_amendment.consequential_correction: If integrated, replace workers footnote final sentence No direct Malkangiri resident perspective was established in this research pass with No direct Malkangiri resident response to the film was established in this research pass. The source study itself still excludes Malkangiri.
recommended_one_amendment.status: Proposal only; no canonical edits. Rout/Behera paragraph already added by root and seen in current draft.

remaining_gaps: No verified direct Malkangiri resident or Adivasi response to the film found in this bounded search.
No claim of broad agreement with either critic.
The Odia-language search did not establish a directly usable resident film response; this is an access/search limit, not evidence no such account exists.
No population-representative study of reception or current2026 healthcare access established.
outcome: Partially fills resident health-access perspective gap; leaves direct resident film reception open.
